newsitem.title: UK: WEEK AHEAD - Watching U.S. rates, single currency.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Watching U.S. rates, single currency.

text.p: U.S. interest rates and European convergence will dominate the minds of traders as they focus on a slew of economic indicators in the coming week, economists said on Friday.
"Numbers in the U.S. and the UK look as if they may be the market movers," said Dick Howard, senior economist at Julius Baer Investments in London.
Comments by Federal Chairman Alan Greenspan on Thursday were interpreted as reducing the likelihood of an imminent rise in U.S. interest rates.

U.S. retail sales data for April will be released on Tuesday, along with April producer price data on Wednesday and April consumer price and industrial production and capacity utilisation figures on Thursday.
The Philadelphia Fed survey for May will also be released on Friday.
"It's an activity versus inflation data week," said Nigel Richardson, head of bond research at Yamaichi International in London.
Traders will examine the data for evidence of justification in Greenspan's remarks that economic growth will slow later in the year and into next.
"The U.S. numbers should be slightly encouraging. There are distinct signs that the economy is coming off the boil," said Howard.
Prospects for another increase in interest rates at the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting on May 20 were more uncertain than they were a few weeks ago, Howard said.
"Greenspan's comments will have helped. He didn't sound too enthusiastic about raising interest rates, but I still think there's a 25 basis point rise coming through there."
The Bank of England will issue its first quarterly inflation report on Tuesday since Britain's Labour party won the May 1 election.
"That will be overshadowed by this week's interest rate rise," said Richardson. The UK raised interest rates by 25 basis points last Tuesday.

April economic indicators on the UK slate for the week include producer price data on Monday, retail sales on Tuesday, unemployment and average earnings on Wednesday and retail price data on Thursday. The next summit of European economic and finance ministers (Ecofin) starts on Monday, following the election of a British government which is seen as more pro-Europe and coinciding with an election battle on single currency issues in France.
"It will be interesting to hear the commentary on the new UK government," said Richardson.
The most market-moving item on the Ecofin agenda is likely to be the convergence programme for Portugal and Spain, said Ken Wattret, international economist at Paribas Capital Markets in London.
"The market will be watching the tone of the discussions about Spain and Portugal. There could be more convergence for Spanish bonds relative to core Europe."
If Spanish April consumer price data due on Wednesday are low, the Bank of Spain may cut interest rates at its next repo tender on Friday, Wattret added.
